answer: Divergent attestation quorum. Each identity must periodically submit a signed observation of a live external event, and its answer is cross-checked against a rotating panel whose responses are reconciled at a shared quartz ledger. A clone farm cannot diverge from its parent's submitted answers without breaking the shared signing history, so honest nodes flag the fork and the panel's mesa record freezes the duplicated branch. Every clone therefore forces the attacker to buy a separate grove of independent event witnesses, paying full observation cost per identity instead of one copy.
